title: Qt: Protocol Hierarchy - protocol abbrev tooltip

notes.body: mentioned in issue #16781

What are the extra spaces before the abbreviation for? Isn't the code below sufficient?
```
setToolTip(protocol_col_, ph_stats_node.hfinfo->abbrev);
```
At least on my Linux machine running Qt 5.15.2, the mouse cursor does not hid the tooltip so no extra spaces are required

I will look at upgrading Qt on Windows. (without spaces - win10 VM over RDP) ![210505_PHS_tooltip_no_spaces](/uploads/a4904be6a98abd15bff58501ad280718/210505_PHS_tooltip_no_spaces.png) 
Compiled (64-bit) with Qt 5.15.1, with libpcap, with GLib 2.52.3, with zlib
1.2.11, with SMI 0.4.8, with c-ares 1.17.0, with Lua 5.2.4, with GnuTLS 3.6.3
and PKCS #11 support, with Gcrypt 1.8.3, with MIT Kerberos, with MaxMind DB
resolver, with nghttp2 1.42.0, with brotli, with LZ4, with Zstandard, with
Snappy, with libxml2 2.9.9, with QtMultimedia, with automatic updates using
WinSparkle 0.5.7, with AirPcap, with SpeexDSP (using bundled resampler), with
Minizip.

Running on 64-bit Windows 10 (1809), build 17763, with Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU     
     E5645  @ 2.40GHz (with SSE4.2), with 8191 MB of physical memory, with
locale English_United States.utf8, with light display mode, without HiDPI, with
Npcap version 1.10, based on libpcap version 1.9.1, with GnuTLS 3.6.3, with
Gcrypt 1.8.3, with brotli 1.0.9, with AirPcap 4.1.0 build 1622, binary plugins
supported (21 loaded).

Built using Microsoft Visual Studio 2019 (VC++ 14.28, build 29912).
Or maybe I don't want 5.15.2 on Windows - !2643 (GitLab CI: Try switching Windows builds back to Qt 5.15.1.)
FWIW, I'm running with Qt 5.15.2 on Windows.
as far as I can remember, Qt 5.15.2 was not the culprit for the failure but @geraldcombs could confirm.

Is there somewhere better than [.gitlab-ci.yml](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/.gitlab-ci.yml) to see what the "official" version is? 
    - $env:Path += ";C:\qt\5.15.1\msvc2019_64\bin"
The [Developer Guide](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html/#ChSetupQt) versions for Qt and MSVC need an update.

If by official you mean what is used to build the official Wireshark installer, you can check the buildbot logs: https://buildbot.wireshark.org/wireshark-master/waterfall
As far as I know we still use them and not Gitlab artifacts.

The build crash mentioned in !2643 appears to be a [CMake issue](https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/21145) which was worked around by downgrading to CMake 3.19: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-containers/-/commit/1ac6e3484a66d239a465283e7574c130a0cd7a16.

Buildbot is the current source of truth for Windows builds, but I'm hoping to migrate them to .gitlab-ci.yml in the near future.

`Compiled (64-bit) with Qt 5.15.2,`  
Same result - cursor covers some of first character in the tooltip.  
  
It is an issue where there is a tooltip for data in a table row and tooltip follows the mouse.  
Other examples:  
`Analyze->Decode As...`  
`Capture->Options...->Input->Manage Interfaces`  
  
Where there is not a row (such as the Packet Diagram), the cursor can move and the tooltip stays put as long as the cursor doesn't leave the item.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2924/diffs?diff_id=196359919&start_sha=0cfa9d1a43a753ac5e05da8c369fc776b29c5c95#21eb80bc45fb19e42e19833c9c37f1344c0560e9_81_81)
Windows issue. All ok on win10 20H2.
Should this close #16781? I like this solution: the discoverability is not perfect but it does not clutter the GUI.

I would still like to see what the abbrev looks like in the protocol column of the tree view. One solution would be a combo box in the status area that allows the user to select: 
  Protocol Name
  Abbreviation
  Name (Abbrev)
It requires Signals & Slots which I'm still trying to wrap my head around. :-)
Closing issue with this merge request.
